task.title: Package the docs for offline reading
task.shortdesc: Write one reader's docs as a static site that opens straight from disk, with no server and no network, to ship with a release, hand to a customer or read on a machine with no access to the docs site.

context.p: opend package builds the docs, filters them for one reader exactly as the previewer and the hosted site do, and writes every page that reader can see. The package holds a page per visible topic, index.html (the first topic), the images and files those topics use, the theme and the logo. Topics and images the reader cannot see are left out, so a package is safe to give to that reader.

Every link is relative and nothing needs scripts, so the pages work from a file:// address, a USB stick or any static web server, in light and dark mode and on narrow screens. The package has no search box, as there is no server to answer it; readers browse the contents or use their browser's find.

step.cmd: Choose who the package is for and package it.

info.p: Name a reader from preview-contexts.yaml, or give their products, features and version. There is no default: a package leaves your machine, so the command refuses to guess and never falls back to the staff view.

stepxmp.codeblock: pnpm opend package path/to/docs --as v2-pro pnpm opend package path/to/docs --product widget --feature sso --version 2.1 --out widget-2.1.zip

stepresult.p: It prints any problems, then wrote .opend/package/<name>.zip (… pages, … files). The zip holds one folder named after the file. A build error writes nothing.

step.cmd: Write a folder instead of a zip file.

info.p: Give --out a path that does not end in .zip. The folder must be new or empty, so an old package is never mixed with a new one.

stepxmp.codeblock: pnpm opend package path/to/docs --as v2-pro --out dist/offline-docs

info.p: Each publication the reader can see is printed for them into pdf/ and linked from the page header. Printing needs headless Chromium, as in ; set OPEND_CHROMIUM_PATH if Playwright's browser is not installed. Links in a PDF to topics outside the publication print as plain text.

postreq.p: --all packages the staff view: everything, with conditions marked. Use it only for your own team. See for every option.
